Exports `ViewPcbComponentEvent` and adds a dedicated Cosmos fixture. `AGENTS.md` instructs contributors not to edit `README.md`; this PR leaves the README unchanged. title: Show JLC price and stock in schematic part details
description: Adds functionality to display JLCPCB part prices and stock availability in the schematic component details tooltip, fetching data from an external API and handling loading states and errors appropriately.
body:
Clicking a schematic component with a JLCPCB part number now fetches its USD unit price and stock from `jlcsearch.tscircuit.com/api/search`. Each part number keeps its existing link and shows an animated loader until the lookup completes.

- Fetch again whenever the details popup opens, without browser caching.
- Match the exact part number and support numeric prices, `price1`, JSON price tiers, and legacy quantity ranges.
- Cancel requests when the popup closes or the selected part changes; stop waiting after 10 seconds. Failed or missing values show “Price unavailable” / “Stock unavailable”.
- Skip lookups for components without JLCPCB part numbers.

Validation:
- Type check, formatting check, and package build pass.
- All 46 tests pass when each test file runs in its own process, including loader, cancellation, selection changes, reopen refresh, failure handling, and API parsing coverage.
- A single-process `bun test` has five existing context-menu failures; reproduced the same five failures on unchanged base commit `62ae619`. The context-menu file passes in isolation.
- Verified a live C1525 lookup and cross-origin response headers. jlcsearch caches responses upstream, so displayed values reflect the latest data served by that service, not a direct live JLCPCB query.

description: Add optional from_connector_pin1_position and to_connector_pin1_position to cad_cable, which are absolute 3D points at each connectors mating face in circuit-world millimeters, computed by the circuit producer, to fix connector roll and identify pin 1.
body:

Their transverse offsets from the cable endpoint centerlines identify pin 1 and fix connector roll.

Core computes these points from footprint pin geometry or motor placement in tscircuit/core#4420. The renderer consumes the resolved points in tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf#240 and no longer performs footprint inference. Existing records can omit both fields and retain legacy orientation.

Tests cover schema round-tripping, unit normalization, finite point validation, absolute/non-unit coordinates, and compatibility with old records. Validation: all 443 Circuit JSON tests pass and the package build/declarations pass.

This supersedes the closed width-direction proposal #876. No merges will be performed on the user's behalf.

title: fix: use relative tolerance in generateArcFromSweep guard
description: Fixes floating-point error in arc generation by adding relative tolerance to semicircular arcs in silkscreen geometry.
body:
## Summary

`generateArcFromSweep` rejects exact semicircular arcs. The guard
`radius < distance / 2` is sensitive to floating-point error: the chord is
computed as `sqrt(dx*dx + dy*dy)`, so an exact semicircle (chord == 2r) can
land a few ULPs above 2r and collapse to a flat two-point chord.

Add a relative tolerance to the comparison and clamp the sqrt radicand with
`Math.max(0, ...)`. Without the clamp the radicand evaluates to a small
negative number and `sqrt` returns `NaN`.

Scope: silkscreen geometry only. No copper, pad, hole, or drill output
changes.

## Effect

C2652953 and C490691 each contain one silkscreen ARC whose chord is exactly
2r. Both rendered as straight two-point lines; both now render as real arcs.

## Tests

- New: `tests/arc-utils-semicircle.test.ts` (7 tests).
- `tests/arc-utils.test.ts` unchanged, no regression.
- Snapshots updated: C2652953 inline, C490691 inline.

title: repro: suffixed VDD pins lack power metadata
description: Fixes missing power metadata for suffixed VDD pins on the USB2517I-JZX component in the EasyEDA converter.
body:
## Motivation

The [USB hub board](https://tscircuit.com/gokul/usb-hub-board) uses the USB2517I-JZX imported from JLCPCB part C478081. The Microchip datasheet identifies `VDD33CR` on pin 24 and `VDD33PLL` on pin 64 as 3.3 V supply inputs.

The converter preserves both pin labels but does not give either pin `requiresPower` metadata because the current power-label inference only accepts digits after `VDD`.


## References

- [USB2517/USB2517I datasheet](https://ww1.microchip.com/downloads/aemDocuments/documents/OTH/ProductDocuments/DataSheets/USB2517-USB2517i-Data-Sheet-00001598C.pdf)
- [JLCPCB C478081](https://jlcpcb.com/partdetail/USB2517I_JZX/C478081)

## Reproduction

| Pin | Current result | Expected semantic role |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 24, `VDD33CR` | No `requiresPower` | 3.3 V supply input |
| 64, `VDD33PLL` | No `requiresPower` | 3.3 V PLL regulator supply input |

![C478081 schematic snapshot](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GokulPandi-M/easyeda-converter/repro-vdd-suffix-power-pins/tests/convert-to-ts/__snapshots__/C478081-power-pin-suffix-repro.snap.svg)

title: Add opt-in supplier availability warnings through parts engine
description: Core can now check supplier stock through the configured parts engine when platform.checkAvailability is explicitly true, providing warnings for components that may not have availability from suppliers.
body:
Core can now check supplier stock through the configured parts engine when platform.checkAvailability is explicitly true. It waits for parts selection, invokes the engine's optional fetchPartAvailability method, and emits source_component_availability_warning saying, for example, “R1 may not have availability from JLCPCB (C1525).” Core no longer calls jlcsearch directly.

- Check every supplier supported by the configured engine. For each supplier, warn only when none of its checked alternatives is confirmed in stock. Zero or unknown stock, failed engine requests, and 10-second timeouts are advisory warnings.
- Engines without the optional method and suppliers returning undefined are skipped. The setting defaults off, and doNotPlace, BOM-disabled, parts-engine-disabled, and DRC-disabled parts are skipped.
- Forward platformFetch and cancellation, share concurrent requests within a circuit, refresh on supplier updates, ignore stale responses, and remove obsolete warnings.
- The engine returns stock, numeric unit price, ISO currency, and an optional lookup timestamp. Core uses stock for warnings; the price remains available to future consumers without adding an availability snapshot element to Circuit JSON.

- https://github.com/tscircuit/props/pull/915 adds the optional engine method, shared stock/price types, and platform setting.
- https://github.com/tscircuit/parts-engine/pull/61 implements the JLC stock/price provider using jlcsearch.
- https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json/pull/877 adds the structured warning.

title: Orient cable plugs and conductors using explicit pin 1 sides
description: Adds startPin1Side and endPin1Side parameters to the cable mesh API to orient cable plugs and conductors based on explicit pin 1 sides, allowing for better control over cable geometry and conductor order during rendering.
body:
Cable plugs can render 90° across their mating header, or reverse contact order while retaining the same width axis. Add `startPin1Side` and `endPin1Side` to the internal cable mesh API: signed directions from connector center toward pin 1, in circuit-world XYZ (+Z up). The first conductor lies on that side at both endpoints.

Seed parallel transport from the starting pin 1 side and distribute the remaining twist by path arc length. Plug geometry and wire sweeps share these frames. Omitted constraints preserve legacy output.

The annotated visual snapshot compares legacy roll, a 90° turn, and a 180° turn, with full cable views and end-plug close-ups. Red is wire 1, so contact order remains visible through each twist.

Tests also measure plug geometry and the actual first conductor cap positions, single endpoint constraints, invalid vectors, and arc-length twist interpolation. Validation: eight targeted cable and visual snapshot tests pass; package build/declarations passed for the implementation.

Consumed by footprint inference in tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gltf#240; integration snapshots and contact-order assertions in tscircuit/core#4420. No new Circuit JSON fields or TSX props. No merges have been performed on the user's behalf.

Component models currently supply colors without material finishes, and the sample exporter drops material metadata. Add approximate surface materials and preserve them through the component APIs and GLB export.

- Share finishes for identified plastic/rubber bodies, leads, contacts, copper pads, connector shells, motor parts, and mechanical metal parts. Tinned leads use metalness 0.8 and roughness 0.55 for subdued reflections.
- Preserve material metadata through the vanilla renderer, align React and vanilla output, and carry cable materials into previews. The browser preview uses component metalness and roughness.
- Keep realistic rendering disabled across CI snapshot paths to avoid its runtime cost. Restore the original test timeouts, remove extra JST supersampling, and refresh standard-rendering snapshots. PoppyGL remains updated to 0.0.34.

Depends on https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-to-gltf/pull/17. The dev dependency pins its published package preview; replace it with a released version before merging. The jscad-fiber minimum is 0.0.89.

Validation: 368 tests across 243 files pass locally in 167.79 seconds, versus 360.70 seconds with realistic rendering (about 54% less time). All nine JST tests also pass after removing extra supersampling. TypeScript, formatting, and diff checks pass. Reviewed 244 refreshed snapshots. GitHub CI timing is pending.

Finishes are visual approximations rather than measured optical properties. Complete PCB renders also need a separate follow-up: circuit-json-to-gltf's footprinter GLB re-import currently discards PBR properties.

title: Add 3D camera presets, GLB downloads, and svg3 model caching
description: Adds 3D camera presets for PNGSVG rendering, enables GLB downloads without requiring svg_type or view, and implements caching for 3D models in the svg3 container.

3D images currently offer a fixed camera, and requesting a rotatable model requires another conversion. Adds `camera_preset` to PNG/SVG rendering and `format=glb` (no `svg_type` or `view` required) to download the same model.

The svg3 container hands the GLB already produced during image rendering to its Durable Object, which stores the binary model in KV before returning the image. Model keys exclude camera, lighting, background, zoom, and raster size while preserving circuit input, project origin, entrypoint, method, and cache version. Images and downloads share a serialized lane, with a short local model cache covering KV propagation lag. GLBs retain cache freshness, size limits, private-request bypass, ETag/HEAD behavior, binary response headers, and CORS for viewers.

Named renderer presets are supported along with `bottom`, `bottom-up`, and `bottom-center-angled`. Both Vercel and Cloudflare adapters preserve binary GLB downloads. API and cache behavior are documented.

title: fix: preserve rectangular plated pad copper dimensions
description: Fixes the copper dimensions of rectangular plated pads during Circuit JSON to Altium export, ensuring accurate representation of pad sizes.
body:
SimpleFOC Shield V3 connector pads P1.1, P2.1, P3.1 and P4.1 shrink from approximately **1.8 × 1.8 mm** copper to **1.6 × 1.6 mm** during Circuit JSON → Altium export. Their approximately **1.2 mm drills** retain the correct size.

The production importer represents these pads as `circular_hole_with_rect_pad` and supplies the copper dimensions in `rect_pad_width` and `rect_pad_height`. For example, P4.1 has:

```json
{
  "shape": "circular_hole_with_rect_pad",
  "rect_pad_width": 1.7999964,
  "rect_pad_height": 1.7999964,
  "hole_diameter": 1.1999976
}
```

The exporter previously read these rectangular dimensions only for `rotated_pill_hole_with_rect_pad`. For circular drills and unrotated slots, it instead looked for `outer_width` / `outer_height`. When those fields and `outer_diameter` were absent, copper width fell back to 1.6 mm and height fell back to that width. The incorrect size was already present in the ASCII intermediate before binary serialization.

Read `rect_pad_width` and `rect_pad_height` first for every plated-hole variant, retaining the existing outer-size and default fallbacks. Width and height remain independent; drill dimensions and slot/pad rotation handling keep their existing mapping. Refresh the affected SimpleFOC Mini snapshot.

Validation:

- A complete round trip of the real Shield board through the production sibling importer and this exporter preserves copper width, height and drill size for all four affected pads.

title: Treat CC2340 bidirectionality as a pin capability
description: Changes the converter to correctly interpret bidirectional GPIO capabilities for CC2340 pins, allowing for proper GPIO function exports without conflicts.
body:
CC2340 datasheet enrichment marks GPIO-capable pins with `isBidirectional: true`. The converter treated that capability as a selected GPIO function and rejected it alongside explicit input/output choices. It also incorrectly treated unconfigured SWD and connected LF crystal pins as GPIO conflicts.

Before, this valid board declaration failed:

```tsx
pinAttributes={{
  pin4: { isGpio: true, isBidirectional: true, isOutput: true },
  pin5: { isGpio: true, isBidirectional: true, isInput: true },
}}
```

After, the same declaration exports GPIO Output on physical pin 4 and Input on physical pin 5. Capability-only SWD pins retain SDK ownership, and the existing crystal connectivity check still selects the LF oscillator. A connected ordinary GPIO without a direction still errors with its component name, physical pin and label:

```text
- U1 pin 5 (DIO12): GPIO direction is missing
```

Pin diagnostics contain one line per pin, without an additional component header or instructions. I2C selection errors remain separate. The converter and CLI error tests use inline snapshots.

Validation:

- 219 tests pass, including eight snapshots; typecheck and formatting pass.
- Official SysConfig 1.28.1 with SimpleLink F3 SDK passes GPIO/I2C native validation, LF crystal round-trip C/header parity, and physical pin-change checks.
- Existing configured pedometer output remains identical when published bidirectional flags are added.

This changes converter interpretation only. No new props, board preset, inferred GPIO direction, metadata edits, or sysconfigts changes. Separate from the merged diagnostics PR #9.

title: Make CC2340 pin configuration errors actionable without generated IDs
description: Connected CC2340 pins without a selected function previously produced generated record IDs and repeated instructions. Report the component name and part number, list each physical pin number and label, and provide one set of instructions for correcting TSX pinAttributes.
body:
Connected CC2340 pins without a selected function previously produced generated record IDs and repeated instructions. Report the component name and part number, list each physical pin number and label, and provide one set of instructions for correcting TSX pinAttributes.

Before:
```text
Unresolved CC2340 pin configuration for U1 (source_component_0, CC2340R52E0RGER):
U1.DIO11 (source_port_3, pin 4): missing or ambiguous selected function...
```

After:
```text
Unresolved CC2340 pin configuration for U1 (CC2340R52E0RGER):
- U1 pin 4 (DIO11): no GPIO direction or supported peripheral selected
- U1 pin 6 (DIO13): no GPIO direction or supported peripheral selected
Update U1's TSX pinAttributes with the intended function for each listed pin: set exactly one of isInput: true or isOutput: true for GPIO, or activeCapability: "i2c_sda" / "i2c_scl" for I2C.
Datasheet capabilities such as isGpio describe what a pin supports; they do not select how this board uses it.
```

Use `toMatchInlineSnapshot()` for the complete missing-function, missing-MCU-port, incomplete-I2C and conflicting-GPIO diagnostics. The regression also verifies that changing generated record IDs leaves the user-facing message unchanged. Validation still fails before partial output is available.

title: Fix native Parasolid exterior region ordering
description: Fixes incorrect native metadata in helical gear X_T exports that caused artifacts when cutting holes in Shapr3D by ensuring the exterior region is correctly ordered and linked in the body-region chain.
body:
Helical gear X_T exports currently point BODY.region at the finite solid region and emit nominal geometry state 0. The [Siemens XT Format Reference](https://ww3.cad.de/foren/ubb/uploads/schulze/XT_Format_April_2008_tcm73-62642.pdf) (printed pp. 87–88) requires the infinite exterior region at the chain head and nominal geometry state 1. These incorrect native metadata produce artifacts when cutting holes in Shapr3D.

Start the body-region chain with the exterior void, link it to the finite solid with reciprocal previous/next links, and emit nominal geometry state 1. Bump the converter to 0.0.4 for downstream consumers.

Add independent OpenCascade cylinder-cut coverage for both gear families, checking valid topology, removed volume, empty hole interiors, retained material, and equivalent merged/unmerged results.

title: Use native entity classes for Parasolid authoring
description: Refactors Parasolid authoring to utilize native entity classes, removing legacy geometry factories and enhancing the repositorys entity management and validation processes.
body:
Parasolid authoring now follows the native entity graph: `Repository` owns typed `Body`, `Region`, `Shell`, `Face`, `Loop`, `Fin`, `Edge`, `Vertex`, `Point`, `Line`, and `Plane` records connected by `EntityReference<T>`. Constructors and named properties support authoring and editing; `Repository.getString()` serializes the graph.

Remove `createParasolidFromPolygons`, `createParasolidFromBodies`, `normalizePolygons`, their geometry input types, and the polygon writer. Geometry validation, vertex welding, T-junction splitting, orientation repair, and coplanar merging belong to [jscad-to-parasolid #2](https://github.com/tscircuit/jscad-to-parasolid/pull/2), which constructs native entities directly. Replace geometry-factory tests with native topology/reference and RGB attribute authoring tests, and document the 0.0.3 API migration. Bulk repository construction now validates and allocates IDs in one pass, avoiding repeated scans on large authored models while retaining editable-ID validation.

Validation: 27 tests pass; typecheck, formatting, and ESM/declaration build pass. Existing lossless parsing, unsupported-schema preservation, character escapes, and entity-ID checks remain covered.

Breaking API change: callers of the removed geometry factories must use the converter or author native entities. No analytic cylinder/curve support is added.

title: Reject invalid transmitted indices and edited entity IDs
description: Rejects nonpositive transmitted indices and revalidates typed record IDs before serialization, ensuring that entity IDs are positive integers and preventing duplicate IDs from being emitted.
body:
A supported X_T record with index `0` is currently passed to `Repository.add`, which treats it as a request for an automatically allocated ID. For example, `82 1 0 42` silently becomes an IntegerArray with ID 1, so canonical serialization changes record identity. Editing a public `entity.id` can also emit zero, negative, fractional, nonfinite, unsafe, or duplicate indices because the existing checks only run during `add`.

Reject nonpositive transmitted indices before constructing records, and revalidate the typed record IDs before either serialization mode. Automatic allocation for newly authored entities is preserved; sparse and out-of-order IDs remain unchanged, and validation never renumbers records or pointers. Unknown suffixes keep their existing opaque round-trip behavior.

The [XT Format Reference](https://ww3.cad.de/foren/ubb/uploads/schulze/XT_Format_April_2008_tcm73-62642.pdf), Logical Layout (printed pp. 4-5), defines transmitted node indices from 1 upwards and reserves pointer 0 for null. These are stream indices, distinct from the separate node-id fields inside some records.

Validation: eight new regression cases fail before the fix. Afterward, all 31 tests / 126 assertions pass, including the independent framing/escape fixtures and existing native-color tests. TypeScript, full formatting, package dry-run and diff checks pass. No native Parasolid-kernel compatibility test is claimed.

AI assistance was used for implementation and tests; the diff, format reference and validation results were reviewed.

title: Repair pinched copper polygons before Palace CAD operations
description: Fixes issues with AM3352 copper polygons that pass Shapely validity but create invalid OpenCASCADE solids due to pinched holes, ensuring proper geometry repairs before Boolean operations.
body:
Stacked on #14 (`dqs-eye-estimate`).

AM3352 copper polygons can pass Shapely validity while extruding into invalid OpenCASCADE solids because a hole touches the exterior or another hole at a single point. Guard Palace prism construction with a bounded local notch before extrusion and record the copper repairs in `geometry-repairs.json` before the expensive Boolean operations. Successful mesh summaries include the same receipt.

The three isolated source reproductions cover top GND (`U1.VSS_OSC_V11` / `pcb_trace_105` / `pcb_via_83`), bottom GND touching antipads, and inner1 `DDR_VREF`. Repairs only remove copper inside a 0.1 µm half-width neighborhood, reject any split into separate polygons, and retain the existing native volume checks.

The reusable converter and the more complete fix for generated antipad footprints are in https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gmsh/pull/1, with independent OpenCASCADE before/after validity checks and TSX/PoppyGL cross-section snapshots. This PR applies the minimal guard to the existing Palace backend; it retains its global Boolean strategy. **Full-board conformal meshing and Palace EM results are still unvalidated**, and this does not claim that every full-board Boolean/resource failure is resolved.

Validation: existing Bun suite 41 pass / 1 skip / 0 fail locally (the unchanged ngspice test requires `SI_PYTHON`); the final native rerun passes all 3 selected tests, including both existing multilayer mesh tests and the new three-case prism regression. TypeScript and Biome pass. No change to the OpenEMS or IBIS/ngspice eye path.

![Actual AM3352 copper without substrate](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gmsh/e4728c51c34fc282a85cb109a6b1e8bbf7d45e95/examples/am3352/mesh-validation/dqs-source-vias-corrected/copper-only.png)

The visualizer opens on this actual-board view, with additional DQS-only and native copper-cutaway views. Reproduction script and camera/input hashes are included.

## Changes

- Save physical boundary triangles and a CAD ownership/volume manifest. Validate linear tetrahedra, orientation/minSICN, material ownership, volume coverage, manifold faces, conformal interfaces, copper-net contacts, drill/cutout intersections, and actual terminal-to-terminal copper connectivity.
- Add `validateMesh`, `createMeshRequirements`, and `validate` CLI usage. Refdes/pin requirements are connectivity checks; missing PCB context is explicitly incomplete. Coincident cross-net nodes are detected even when their node tags differ.
- Add TSX-generated differential through-via/stub and cutout cases, PoppyGL snapshots, and independent saved-MSH corruption tests. Extend the visualizer with the new views.
- Add recorded crop bounds/route corridors, slab partitioning, optional Netgen optimization, and optional contour approximation with distance/area receipts. Contours remain exact by default; all copper within the analysis domain stays included.
- Retain the exact AM3352 input compressed, stackup assumptions, source-via quality comparisons, resource-failure receipts, and a 42-solid first-interface subset for further partition diagnosis.

## Validation

- 26 native tests pass, including snapshot comparisons and corruption cases for missing/disconnected interfaces, inverted/nonmanifold cells, missing materials, shorts with shared or duplicated node tags, filled drills/cutouts, and a broken inner-layer copper path.
- TypeScript, Biome, Ruff, and the Cosmos static build pass. CLI success and quality-failure exit codes verified.
- All three actual AM3352 source-via meshes pass a fresh independent recheck. The expanded crop fixes the 0.12 µm barrel-cap sliver: minimum minSICN improves from 0.000502 to 0.002009, and the new mesh passes a 0.001 gate. It contains 181,224 tetrahedra; export plus validation took 201.46 seconds. All 114 CAD solids independently pass OpenCASCADE validity.

## Remaining scope

The complete-route corridor produces 523 independently valid CAD solids in about 30 seconds, but conformal partitioning remains slow: its first stage took 665 seconds and the diagnostic was explicitly stopped during the second stage after 1,273 seconds. No successful full-route mesh is claimed. The saved subset and input make that bottleneck reproducible.

These checks establish mesh consistency, not EM convergence, air-domain boundaries, Palace port apertures, or routing/eye quality. See the [README](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gmsh/blob/validate-dqs-mesh/README.md) and [actual-board evidence](https://github.com/tscircuit/circuit-json-to-gmsh/tree/validate-dqs-mesh/examples/am3352/mesh-validation).

body:
The AM3352 Palace CAD failures were receiving invalid OpenCASCADE solids even though their 2D polygons passed GEOS validity checks. This adds a reusable circuit-json → Gmsh converter, isolated source reproductions, and TSX-generated native CAD and PoppyGL snapshot regressions.

- Preserve layer stackups, copper outlines, plated barrels, drill voids, and dielectric materials. Provide CLI/library exports, optional conformal tetrahedral meshing, and native triangle previews with cutaways and cross sections.
- Replace generated bounding-box antipads with offsets of actual per-layer copper footprints. This removes the five touching-hole artifacts in the bottom GND foil.
- Detect genuine point contacts before extrusion. Apply an audited 0.1 µm half-width local copper-removal notch, reject disconnected results, and independently validate the isolated before/after BReps with OpenCASCADE. Strict mode rejects the same inputs and writes reproductions.
- Include original/fixed AM3352 top GND, bottom GND, and inner1 DDR_VREF solids with source identifiers, coordinates, provenance, and repair receipts.

Validation: 7 Bun tests pass with native Gmsh/OpenCASCADE and nonblank PoppyGL image comparisons; TypeScript, Biome, Ruff, CLI smoke test, generated examples, and the Cosmos gallery build pass locally. The full AM3352 CAD assembly produced 5,572 solids in 288.35 s with 11.7 GiB peak RSS and matching expected/native volume. **That benchmark is CAD assembly only: full-board conformal meshing and a Palace EM solve remain unvalidated.** The original full-size Boolean exception was not reproduced in a minimal case; the independent BRep checks demonstrate the invalid inputs and the repairs.

Repo bootstrapped through https://github.com/tscircuit/create-repo/pull/88 using Bun and @tscircuit/plop per the handbook. No npm publication in this PR.
